aiOverview.content: Utah State University (USU) is primarily located in Logan, Utah, where its main academic, research, and residential campus spans 600 acres at the mouth of Logan Canyon. As a public land-grant institution, USU maintains a massive presence across the state with 30 total locations, including residential campuses in Price (USU Eastern) and Blanding. Main Campus: Logan The Logan campus is situated approximately 81 to 85 miles north of Salt Lake City in the Cache Valley, nestled against the Wasatch and Bear River mountains. It is characterized by its "bench" location—a foothill overlooking the valley to the west—and is home to more than 100 buildings, including the landmark Old Main. Expand map Zoom in Zoom out Key Locations and Regions While Logan is the central hub, USU operates a statewide system to ensure accessibility across Utah. Residential Campuses: Logan: The largest public residential campus in Utah. USU Eastern (Price): Joined the system in 2010; serves as a residential junior college. Blanding: A residential campus located near the four-borders region in southern Utah. Statewide Campus Regions: Northern: Brigham City, Kaysville, Tremonton, and Salt Lake City. Central/Southwest: Nephi, Delta, Ephraim, Richfield, and St. George. Uintah Basin: Roosevelt and Vernal. Southeastern: Moab, Monticello, and Monument Valley. Specialized Centers: Includes the Swaner Preserve and EcoCenter in Park City and the Utah Botanical Center in Kaysville.
